To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calcium depletion via EDTA results in a loss of a distinct basement membrane and an increase in the width of the T tubule.
calcium removal causes a loss of the basement membrane and an increase in the size of the T tubules.
calcium-free EDTA bathing causes a loss of the basement membrane and a widening of T tubules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of extracellular matrix in the control of water and calcium distribution in skeletal muscle.
the role of calcium and the basement membranes in muscle contraction.
the fine structure of amphibian muscle following calcium removal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium-free EDTA bath caused a loss in the integrity of the muscle fibers and the loss of calcium from the fibers.
calcium-free EDTA bath causes a decrease in muscle volume, a decrease in muscle mass, a decrease in the number of mitochondria and an increase in the width of T tubules.

the loss of calcium from muscle fibers in vitro causes a marked increase in the diameter of the T tubule, a loss of the basement membrane, a decrease in the number of mitochondria, and an increase of the number of myofilaments in the I bands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the basement membrane is not a static barrier to the movement of calcium ions into and out of muscle, but rather a dynamic membrane which is involved in the regulation of calcium and other ions.
the calcium-free EDTA bath removes calcium from the muscle and causes a swelling of the T tubules, but does not cause a significant swelling of the myofibrillar elements.
EDTA is not an ideal agent for the removal of calcium from muscle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the basement membrane is a dynamic structure that is affected by calcium and water efflux.
the basement membrane of the extensor muscle of Rana is a highly dynamic structure, and that it is capable of changing its morphology in response to changes in the environment of the muscle.
the loss of calcium from the muscle leads to an increase in T-tubule width.
